hook: The genius behind alternating current, radio control and the Tesla coil.

pages.x: Nikola Tesla was born at midnight during a lightning storm in 1856, in Smiljan, in today's Croatia, the son of a Serbian priest. A family legend says the midwife called him a child of the storm, and his mother answered: "No, of light."

He could memorise whole books, and pictured machines in his mind so clearly that he could build and test them there before making them. At college in Graz he gambled away his money and left without a degree.
In 1882, walking in a park in Budapest and reciting poetry, he suddenly saw how to make a motor run on alternating current. He drew it in the sand with a stick.
pages.fx: His induction motor still drives most of the machines in the world, from fans and pumps to factories.

pages.x: In 1884 he arrived in New York with four cents in his pocket, and went to work for Edison. Tesla said he was promised 50,000 dollars to improve Edison's machines, and when he did, Edison laughed that it was a joke. He quit.

Westinghouse bought his patents. Alternating current could carry power over long distances. It lit up the Chicago World's Fair in 1893, and in 1896 power from Niagara Falls reached Buffalo. It powers the world today.
In 1898 in New York he steered a model boat by radio. People watching thought it was magic, or that a trained monkey was hidden inside. He also invented the Tesla coil.
pages.fx: Remote control, and much of radio, grew from ideas like his.

pages.x: In 1899 in Colorado Springs he built a giant coil that threw artificial lightning bolts dozens of metres long. He also thought he had picked up signals from Mars.

He dreamed of sending messages and power through the air around the world, free. He began a giant tower on Long Island, but his backer, the banker J. P. Morgan, stopped paying. The tower was torn down.
In old age he lived alone in New York hotels, in debt, feeding the pigeons in the parks. He said he loved one white pigeon as a man loves a woman. He died poor in 1943.
Tesla's alternating current system powers the world. A unit of magnetism, the tesla, is named after him, and so is a car company.
pts: Made alternating current the world's power system
A pioneer of radio and remote control
